name: Tom Collins
description: Gin sour lengthened with soda—tall, lemony, and quietly elegant.
history: A 19th-century Collins variation associated with Old Tom gin historically, though modern versions often use London dry or contemporary gins.
whyItWorks: The sour core (gin, lemon, sugar) is refreshed by carbonation. Ice and soda keep it sessionable.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice.
Strain into a Collins glass filled with ice.
Top with club soda and lift gently with a spoon.
Garnish with lemon (and cherry if you like).
techniqueNotes: Shake the sour components; do not shake the soda.
Fever-Tree club soda keeps the finish clean.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Bright juniper that stays lively in a long drink.
Adds tea spice interest to a classic Collins.
Softer floral Collins—pair with cucumber if desired.

variations.name: Falernum Gin Collins
variations.notes: Use falernum instead of plain syrup.
